static_traits.name: Chen Jin
static_traits.family_status: Has a supportive family, but has not yet shared feelings of inadequacy and self-doubt with the family
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with colleagues become strained due to self-doubt and comparison
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems in the past; has not received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: At the first consultation, slightly nervous but actively cooperative; clear expression, strong logic; able to self-reflect and distinguish reason from emotion ('I rationally know I cannot save everyone, but emotionally it is hard to accept')

basic_info.main_problem: I feel that working in a large hospital, I can never save enough lives, which gives me feelings of inadequacy and self-doubt.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of inadequacy are affecting my work performance and overall health. And it would help me if I could stop comparing myself excessively with others.
growth_experiences: After starting work at a large hospital, the client set very high expectations for themselves and often compared their influence with other doctors; over time, this self-doubt gradually worsened, especially after difficult cases or poor outcomes.

A recent event of losing a patient became a turning point, markedly intensifying self-doubt and feelings of inadequacy; afterward, when handling difficult cases or when poor outcomes occurred, the thought 'I am not good enough, I did not do enough' frequently surfaced.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough / not good enough
Only by saving every patient do I have value

special_situations.event: 最近失去一位患者的事件
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot save every patient, it means I have failed and I am not competent enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to focus attention on positive results once achieved, to relieve feelings of inadequacy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I did not fulfill my duty; I am not good enough

special_situations.event: While on duty, seeing a colleague praised for successfully handling a difficult case
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others do better and receive praise, it means I am not as good as them
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently compares with others to spur the self on, while not sharing these feelings of inadequacy with family to maintain an image
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do better than me; I am falling behind

special_situations.event: After difficult cases or adverse outcomes occur
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the outcome does not meet the ideal standard, it proves I did not do enough and am not capable enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuously ruminating on failure experiences, ignoring successful cases to 'urge oneself on'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am destined to be unable to save enough lives

special_situations.event: When reviewing work results, losses and failures are more readily noticed, and success cases are overshadowed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only continuous and comprehensive success counts; individual positive results are insufficient to prove worth
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negates positive feedback, regarding others' gratitude and own contributions as 'not important'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These successes do not count; I am still not good enough

core_conflict.wish: Longs to save all patients and be recognized as a fully competent doctor with major influence
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure and powerlessness, being rated as not good enough and incompetent and losing value and recognition
defense_goal: Maintains extremely high standards and strict self-monitoring to avoid being evaluated as incompetent, and maintains a sense of safety and control by comparing with others and suppressing vulnerability

object_relations.self_representation: A doctor who is inadequate and constantly needs to prove oneself
object_relations.object_representation: More successful and judgmental colleagues/authoritative others

object_relations.self_representation: A responsible healer who longs for one's contributions to be seen
object_relations.object_representation: Vulnerable patients who need to be saved and grateful family members

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor discusses topics such as 'defining success' and 'the realistic boundaries of medicine (not every patient can be saved)'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to use rational and conceptual explanations to control uncomfortable emotions, viewing the acknowledgment of realistic limits as possibly lowering self-standards (transference: replacing emotional contact with rationality)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses objective, data-based language with a steady tone, reducing expression of emotional vocabulary and subjective feelings; mainly analytical question-and-answer, avoiding going deeply into emotional experience.

manifestations: Working in a large hospital, frequently facing patient death and the limits of medicine directly
Takes 'saving every patient' as the ideal standard, finding it hard to accept outcomes beyond control
After losing a patient, self-doubt and feelings of inadequacy markedly intensify
outcomes: Self-worth highly tied to outcomes and wavering
Increased work pressure and risk of occupational burnout

manifestations: Positive results are overshadowed by losses and failures, making it hard to feel the positive meaning of work
The experience of one's personal contribution eroded by the belief that it is 'never enough'
outcomes: Decreased sense of achievement and increased self-doubt
Enjoyment of life is impaired (such as difficulty enjoying rowing and vacations)

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizing 'success = saving every patient' as a rigid self-demand
Evaluating self-worth by perfectionist standards, ignoring realistic boundaries and complexity

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-criticism ('I am not good enough', 'I am falling behind')
While on duty, constantly compares with colleagues, lowering self-evaluation
Unwilling to share feelings of inadequacy and vulnerability with family

exception_events.target_problem: After difficult cases or poor outcomes, the client usually falls into strong feelings of inadequacy and self-doubt, believing they 'did not do enough'.
exception_events.unique_outcome: After successfully treating a young girl with severe pneumonia, the patient recovered and the family expressed sincere thanks; the client can clearly recall and acknowledge that they had a positive impact.
exception_events.reason: Clues: this case had clear treatment effects and external positive feedback (thanks from family members), making it easier for the client to see concrete contributions and controllable factors, thereby briefly weakening the narrative of 'never enough'.

positive_force: Has professional ability and experience and evidence of successfully treating patients
Has supportive family resources (though has not yet asked for help)
Clear logic, able to distinguish controllable from uncontrollable factors
Willing to self-reflect and proactively seek help; positive attitude
negative_force: Perfectionism and all-or-nothing standards rigidly bind self-worth to outcomes
Excessively comparing with colleagues and seeking external validation lead to fluctuations in self-evaluation
Negating positive outcomes, focusing on failure (mental filtering and disqualifying the positive)
Negative prediction and catastrophizing tendencies strengthen the sense of inadequacy
Remains avoidant about expressing vulnerability (not sharing with family), aggravating inner loneliness and stress

target_behavior.behavior: Strong self-denial and anxiety after difficult cases or poor outcomes
antecedent: Case progression is unsatisfactory or adverse outcomes occur
target_behavior.core_reason: Defines success as 'must save every patient', and rigidly binds outcomes to self-worth with all-or-nothing thinking and catastrophizing.
target_behavior.function: Maintains high standards and a sense of control through self-punishment and high vigilance, attempting to avoid further failure.
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance is affected, emotional burden increases, further weakening self-confidence and efficiency.

target_behavior.behavior: Comparing oneself with colleagues while on duty and lowering self-evaluation
antecedent: Scenes of colleagues successfully handling difficult cases
target_behavior.core_reason: Seeks external validation and comparison to locate self-worth, influenced by the cognitions of 'comparing and despairing' and 'mind reading'.
target_behavior.function: Gains direction or motivation through comparison in the short term, but essentially avoids inner insecurity.
target_behavior.consequence: Relationships with colleagues are strained, self-doubt intensifies, affecting teamwork and career development.

target_behavior.behavior: Decreased enjoyment of leisure activities (such as rowing, being unable to relax on vacation)
antecedent: Even while resting, still ruminates on failures and losses at work
target_behavior.core_reason: Negative emotions and self-criticism occupy attentional resources, leading to experiential avoidance and behavioral inhibition.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the reactivation of guilt and feelings of failure by reducing investment in leisure.
target_behavior.consequence: Quality of life declines, recovery and regulation functions are impaired, further affecting work and interpersonal relations.
